answer: Mutual-credit clearing: each identity must post a quartz-signed trade receipt with a distinct counterparty before its next transaction clears. A knoll of verified receipts, one per counterparty, gates throughput, so fresh identities stall until real trading partners sign. Attacker cost is the working capital locked in genuine bilateral trades plus the overhead of sustaining many counterparties; a haven of reused signers collapses when receipts are cross-checked.
